rationale.conceptual: The method involves a self-consistent Hartree-Fock mean-field theory with spinor degrees of freedom, solving a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation and a noncondensate density matrix self-consistently. It requires careful understanding of the many-body formalism, iterative numerical implementation, and phase boundary root-finding. Not a textbook exercise, but not a radically novel algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of three sequential steps: build solver module, compute AFM-FM boundary CSV, compute BA-P boundary CSV. I/O is straightforward, with no external data fetching or complex tooling. Implementation uses only NumPy/SciPy, making orchestration simple.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a self-consistent Hartree-Fock solver for a spin-1 Bose gas, which involves non-trivial many-body theory and iterative numerical techniques (conceptual 3). The pipeline is simple (2-3 steps, CSV output, standard libraries) causing low execution difficulty (2). Resource needs are minimal: CPU-only, no large data, small memory.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Uniform system self-consistent equations are solved for a few hundred parameter points (temperatures, Zeeman energies) on a single CPU core; no large datasets or heavy linear algebra.
